contents: A whole forward crawl, not one page. 6 pages, 436 events total (80/80/80/80/80/36), horizon 2026-08-09T15:00:00Z -> 2026-10-10T16:00:00Z. Page 6's pages.newer is null, which is the termination condition Stage 0.7's fetchMatches relies on. Captured under hl=en-US, matching the identity locale the client pins — unlike rest_getSchedule.json, there is no known locale discrepancy here.
whyThisFixtureExists: rest_getSchedule.json (2026-08-09) is one unparameterised call and covers ~5 days. Stage 0.7 makes fetchMatches follow data.schedule.pages.newer until it is null, and nothing in the tree proved that terminates or exercised the multi-page code path. This corpus is that proof: it is a measurement of one crawl (page count and horizon are NOT expected constants — see recapture.crawl below), asserted in tests/fixture-crawl.test.ts. It carries no per-match edge-case assertions on purpose; those stay on rest_getSchedule.json, which is the only fixture with the future-dated-yet-completed row and the exact TBD/lossy-state counts a fresh capture cannot reproduce (see fixtures/REQUIREMENTS.md).

verification.termination: verified 2026-08-12 by crawling to exhaustion: page 6 of 6 has pages.newer === null.
verification.contiguity: verified 2026-08-12, exhaustive over this one crawl: page spans are ascending and non-overlapping, and the 436 match ids are pairwise distinct across all six pages. Asserted in tests/fixture-crawl.test.ts, not only stated here.
verification.pageWidthIsNotTime: page 6 alone spans a month (2026-09-10 -> 2026-10-10) while page 1 spans four days; a page is 80 events, never a time range. Basis: this one crawl.

recaptureNotes.note: Re-derive with `npm run capture -- getSchedule <dir> --crawl`, never by replaying pages.newer from this capture. pageToken decodes to newer::<snowflake>; a snowflake from 2026-08-12 selects a slice of history that no longer sits on a page boundary once the schedule has moved on, so a replayed token is a different request that only looks like a reproduction. `pagesCaptured` (6) and `horizonUtc` are what THIS crawl happened to reach, not a contract — a recapture that takes 5 pages or 9, or reaches a different horizon, is not a failure. What must still hold: termination (some page has pages.newer === null), contiguity, and no duplicate match id across pages — see tests/fixture-crawl.test.ts.
